scenes.name: 周天下
scenes.scene: Broad stone courtyard before a restrained Zhou ceremonial hall. Delegations of independent Chinese princes and envoys in distinct but muted ceremonial robes stand together in a horizontal line before a raised bronze ritual vessel at center, discussing an unlettered rolled covenant. A distant enthroned ruler visible through the open hall is small and subordinate to the gathering. Quiet ranks of attendants and bare cloth standards recede at either side, distant hills behind palace roofs. Morning gold and atmospheric blue, solemn negotiated order and shared rites; avoid everyone kneeling to an absolute conqueror.

scenes.name: 朝廷
scenes.scene: An investiture audience in a modest Chinese timber hall. In a horizontal mid-distance group a seated senior sovereign and two court officials present a plain pale jade ceremonial tablet to a standing recipient in a dark robe, with a small unlettered seal casket on a low table between them. Side rows of officials and a discreet city representative suggest different political ranks. Restrained dignified ritual, dark crimson wood and golden diffuse light. No enormous imperial crown, no fantasy regalia, no legible documents. Faces and jade tablet all close to one horizontal midline; show the architecture above and floor below for safe cropping.

scenes.name: 礼教
scenes.scene: Six Chinese scholars of differing ages and personalities, dressed in sober earth-tone, indigo and grey historical robes, calmly debate at a broad low table in an open scholarly pavilion. One unfurls an unlettered scroll; another gestures toward a simple diagram-less wood counting board; a modest bronze ritual vessel stands beside books. No literal icons for schools and no religious god figures. Garden and distant town visible outside, pale afternoon light with warm concentrated light on the six faces and hands. Mood is differing schools of statecraft sharing one intellectual tradition. All six figures across the center, not tightly crowded.

scenes.name: 学宫
scenes.scene: A living Chinese academy in a hillside town: at center an elder teacher and a small group of adult students discuss an open book whose pages have no readable text, seated beneath the deep eaves of a timber lecture hall. To one side, two travelling scholars carry cloth-wrapped book bundles toward the gate, suggesting the mobility of learning. A courtyard, modest tiled library and bamboo grove stretch horizontally behind. Gentle green-grey and amber, reflective light, warm human dignity, no spectacular religious shrine or huge Buddha statue. Keep teacher, students and travelers in a shallow middle band.
